title: Cue Factory — sketchbook for prompt generation & provenance
content:
Purpose:
This is a fast-moving sketchbook for a modular prompt factory: generate, label, and triage small cue variants (single-shot, multi-shot, directive permutations) then measure provenance and failure modes across model variants.

Why: quick way to create coverage for brittle instruction phrasing, token-budget tradeoffs, and to produce evaluation prompt-sets that are traceable back to the generating heuristic. Useful for automated A/B style rollouts in the console or for building offline eval corpora.

High-level goals:
- Small, composable cue pieces (role, constraint, example, output-format) that can be recombined automatically.
- Attach provenance metadata to each variant (seed-rule, heuristics used, date, author).
- Produce few-shot sets optimized for either precision (conservative answers) or recall/creativity depending on task.
- Capture failure signatures (hallucination, truncation, instruction-ignoring) and map to cue attributes.

Core mechanics (conceptual):
1) Template components: role_prompt | context_blurb | instruction | examples_block | output_spec. Each is a short string; the factory composes permutations.
2) Heuristic operators: paraphrase(n), abridge(max_tokens), anchor_with_example(i), invert_temperature_hint. Operators record their action in provenance.
3) Variant scoring: quick metrics from model run (token count, latency, exact-match on synthetic assertions, confidence proxies like repetition).

Canonical template (example):
- role_prompt: "You are a concise technical assistant trained to explain code and reasoning."
- context_blurb: "Given the user query and short code snippet below."
- instruction: "Explain why the following code fails and provide a minimal fix."
- examples_block (1-shot):
  Example 1 input: ... output: ...
- output_spec: "Answer in 3 bullets, then show a one-line fixed snippet."

Few-shot sets (experiments):
A) Precision set (P-set): 3 examples that are short, high-signal, and all use the explicit <FIXED> token to mark the fix. Goal: reduce hallucination of unrelated fixes.
B) Divergent set (D-set): mixed tones, one deliberately ambiguous example to coax creative but risky outputs. Used to probe recall/creativity tradeoffs.
C) Edge-case set (E-set): contrived tokenization traps (weird unicode, long identifier names) to probe truncation and alignment with token budget.

Concrete few-shot example (P-set) — inline: 
--PROMPT START--
You are a concise technical assistant. Explain WHY the code below throws a TypeError and provide a one-line fix. Use exactly 3 bullets, then one code line with the fix wrapped in <FIXED> tags.

Input:
function add(a, b) { return a + b }
console.log(add('2', 2))

Expected output:
- Bullet 1: brief cause (type mismatch)
- Bullet 2: where it happens (string + number in console.log)
- Bullet 3: consequence (implicit coercion)
<FIXED>console.log(add(Number('2'), 2))</FIXED>
--PROMPT END--

Notes: this rigid output spec intentionally reveals model strain — good probe for format fidelity.

Observed failure modes (running on x-model variants):
- Format drift: model emits explanation but forgets to include <FIXED> wrapper ~12% of runs (temperature dependent).
- Over-explaining: some variants add long context paragraphs, breaking the 3-bullet constraint.
- Token truncation: examples with long identifier names sometimes cause the final fix to be clipped if examples_block is too large.

Heuristic experiments to try (quick list):
- anchor_with_example(positive): prepend a minimal example that exactly matches output_spec to prime format fidelity.
- abridge(50): reduce context_blurb to 50 tokens to test truncation margins.
- paraphrase(2): create 2 paraphrases of the instruction and measure variance.
- prefix-with-role-strength: add phrases like 'You MUST output only the requested sections.' and measure compliance and hallucination.

Provenance tagging (minimal fields to store alongside each variant):
- generator_id: e.g., cue-factory:v0.3
- operators: comma-separated list (anchor_with_example, abridge50, paraphrase2)
- seed_rule: human label (e.g., 'precision-single-fix')
- created_by: name
- created_at: ISO date
(We keep these as plain strings for the prototyping DB.)

Failure triage rubric (quick):
- If format drift > 5%: try anchor_with_example + low-temp baseline.
- If hallucination (invented function names/behavior) increases: reduce ambiguity in examples, add explicit constraints on out-of-scope content.
- If truncation occurs: move examples to external context reference (shorten in-prompt and supply appended snippet via file handle in future private deployments).

Adversarial probes to add to E-set:
- Strings that look like code but include invisible unicode (zero-width joiners) to see tokenization effects.
- Very long single-word identifiers to stress kv-cache and attention planning.
- Reversed examples: show example output first then input to see if ordering matters.

Quick experiment log (scratch):
- 2024-06-05: seed run on hosted-api-beta with cue-factory:v0.2; P-set format fidelity 88% (temp 0.2).
- 2024-06-10: added anchor_with_example improved to 96% but added slight verbosity. Logged under JIRA-4582.
- 2024-06-18: E-set found truncation on long id names on dedicated-small; filed platform note to SRE (see gh:infra/kv-cache#7).

Open questions / TODOs (prioritized):
- [P0] Define minimal provenance schema we can store in Redwood Console without blowing up index size. (ask infra for storage budget).
- [P1] Implement a small generator script that emits 100 variants and exports CSV with provenance and token counts (Liam to pair).
- [P2] Add automation to map failures to recommended operator transforms (e.g., if format drift -> automatically try anchor_with_example and abridge).
- [P3] Decide if we want to ship a CLI to produce variants for customers to run in Private deployments.

Notes to self (style & heuristics):
- Favor composable short fragments over long monolith prompts. Easier to trace which fragment caused a failure.
- Keep examples in few-shot compact and highly consistent with desired output format.
- Use simple explicit tokens (<FIXED>, <JSON>, <BULLET>) to increase parse reliability.

References:
- Related: gh: redwood-inference/prompt-evals (seed corpora)
- See also: confluence page 'Prompt Eval Deck' (linked above)

Immediate next steps:
1) Liam to prototype generator script and push minimal CSV by 2024-06-12.
2) Run A/B across hosted/dedicated for P-set and E-set; capture format fidelity, avg tokens, and max latency.
3) Short write-up for product-hosted-api to test rollout experiments (one-pager).

Rough TODO (personal):
- Move promising transforms into gh:cues/transformations as small functions.
- Add a short README in repo with examples of canonical template and provenance fields.
- Pair with Nora for edge-case unicode probes.

--end of sketchbook page--
